Week 10: Real Review Forms and Cases

Published requirements, reported measurements, and a separate studio track

Use this with the Week 10 slides and flipped practice card. Choose one claim to inspect. The short classroom exercise does not qualify you to judge an entire paper or approve a building.

Read the labels: the forms below are actual published requirements; the paper results come from published studies; the exercises and studio questions are course adaptations. No classroom comment below is presented as an actual peer review of either paper. Sources checked 18 November 2026; the named editions are deliberate.

Real Review Forms

NeurIPS 2026: distinguish dimensions, recommendation and confidence

Official Main Track Handbook, Review Form, version V2026.3.

Reviewers supply a summary, contribution type, reasoned strengths/weaknesses, limitations and actionable questions. The four dimensions are Quality, Clarity, Significance and Originality; their interpretation depends on contribution type. The form requests ideally 3–5 questions and what answers could change the evaluation. Requested experiments should address a stated question and be feasible.

Actual scale Meaning
Each dimension: 1–4 Poor, fair, good, excellent
Overall: 1–6 Strong reject, reject, borderline reject, borderline accept, accept, strong accept
Confidence: 1–5 From an educated guess to strong familiarity and careful checking

Course use: write one consequential question and a condition for changing your advice. Do not average the scales into a “scientific validity” score. A confident reviewer can still be wrong; explain the check behind the confidence.

ACM CHI 2026: contribution and a revision list

Official guide, “The Review Form”.

The form asks for the HCI contribution, an expertise rating (1–4), and assessment of significance, originality, research quality, clarity and prior work. Reviewers must specify required revisions.

Actual recommendation Meaning
A Accept with minor revisions
ARR Either A or revise and resubmit
RR Revise and resubmit
RRX Either RR or reject
X Reject

Course use: distinguish a required correction from a desirable extension. Finish with “I can verify this revision by looking at ___.” CHI’s codes describe publication options; they are not percentages, architectural performance measures or A4 marks.

PLOS ONE: can the evidence support the conclusion?

Actual review-form PDF, pp. 1–2 · publication criteria.

Is the manuscript technically sound, and do the data support the conclusions?

Other form questions address statistical analysis, underlying data availability and intelligible presentation; the reviewer explains the answers in written comments. PLOS ONE evaluates scientific validity without selecting on perceived importance.

Course use: identify a claim you could check without agreeing that the topic is fashionable. For a qualitative or design contribution, specify appropriate evidence; do not demand a statistical test merely because another study type uses one.

What can be borrowed across the forms?

Use this short sequence for the class exercise, rather than pretending there is one universal journal form:

  1. Readback: what is the contribution or decision?
  2. Evidence: where exactly is its support?
  3. Challenge: which missing definition, comparison or condition matters?
  4. Revision: what must change, and what observation would resolve it?
  5. Scope: what did you inspect, and what remains unchecked?

If practising a full venue form later, use that venue’s current instructions and review the whole submission. Today’s excerpt review ends with a bounded evidence judgment, not an accept/reject verdict on the paper.

Paper Track

Case A: layout generation — which metric is being improved?

Nauata et al. (2021), House-GAN++: Generative Adversarial Layout Refinement Network towards Intelligent Computational Agent for Professional Architects. Official CVPR paper.

Author preprint, Table 2 is an alternate open reading link.

Read: metric definitions in §3 (p. 13634), protocol in §5 (p. 13636), and Table 2 (p. 13639). The slide reproduces the two Ours_dyna rows, labelled Divers. and Compat. in the paper. These compare dynamic refinement with different optimization targets. The reported ± is across-round standard deviation, not a confidence interval or a building pass mark.

Course-authored reviewer task: use both columns to explain the trade-off. Then choose one architectural requirement the table cannot establish—such as a usable circulation route—and specify the drawing or test you would need. Do not infer accessibility, daylight or construction feasibility from image/graph metrics alone.

Case B: thermal images — what does a screening threshold establish?

Mora & Bardhan (2025), Towards carbon neutrality: mapping mass retrofit opportunities in Cambridge, UK, Royal Society Open Science 12:241337. Publisher · open manuscript PDF.

Read: §2.2.3 and §3.1.3, Figure 6, and §4.4 (PDF pp. 7, 10, 14–15). The study uses wall ΔT >2°C as its criterion for higher retrofit need. It reports 18 of 25 cases in that category. This is a study-specific screening rule, not an established building standard.

Definition check: the main text does not fully specify the temperature reference used for ΔT. Do not rename it wall–air or indoor–outdoor difference. Supplement Table S3 is a follow-up reading, not something this exercise has already verified.

Course-authored reviewer task: locate the measurement definition and conditions; ask what evidence justifies the cutoff and whether uncontrolled heating changes classification. Separate “prioritise further investigation” from “establish retrofit need.” Missing information in the excerpt is a request to investigate, not proof that the entire study is invalid.

Ten-minute exercise: choose A or B

Time Do this Write or mark
0–3 min, individually Open the specified table/sections. Locate one claim and the reported measurement. Metric, units or scale, direction, test conditions and exact source location
3–7 min, compare Each person states what the result supports. Identify one disagreement or missing check. One supported statement and one unresolved question
7–10 min, agree a request Specify a proportionate correction, additional evidence or narrower claim. Required action, completion evidence and what would change your advice

Submit to your own notes: a short inspection record. Use “supported within this comparison,” “problem found,” or “not established,” with a reason. Do not assign a journal verdict based on this excerpt. You are not expected to run a new model or collect new building data in ten minutes.

For a research-oriented A4 review, transfer this method to one result from the author’s actual workflow: check its definition, comparison and claimed scope. The published cases supply models of what to question, not thresholds to copy into your project.

Studio Track

Published design-review requirements

Mid Sussex Design Review Panel Terms of Reference, approved 24 January 2018, pp. 1 and 5: five criteria—architectural integrity, context, environmental performance, character and detail. Its recommendations are support / support with amendments / object; the panel advises rather than makes planning decisions.

Design Commission for Wales, Design Review Essentials, 2020 document, p. 1: bring a brief, location/site analysis, plans, sections and elevations. One actual prompt is:

How has your site analysis informed the design?

These are published UK design-review examples. They are not Hong Kong regulations, project-specific compliance checks or the A4 marking rubric.

A real panel request: Creigiau Phase 5B

DCFW report: Land North of J33 M4 – Phase 5B, Cardiff. Review held 21 May 2026; report issued 5 June 2026. Official report page · Publisher’s PDF.

Read p. 5: the panel requests “clearer evidence of the design process undertaken” and sections explaining key boundary relationships. On p. 8 it also requests illustrative material to assess residents’ everyday experience. These are documented requests from the panel, not invented classroom feedback.

Course task: compare two versions of your own project, mark one consequential change, and draw a section through the affected boundary. Explain the benefit, trade-off and remaining question. The task adapts the report’s evidence request; it is not the panel’s wording or a compliance test.

Reading route: use the case note above for the short exercise. Open the official report page for the complete document and its context; the separate PDF link is an alternative.

Curated questions for your studio project

The questions and adequacy checks below are course adaptations of those criteria. Choose one row, then inspect a consequential drawing or result. A rendering alone may not answer the question.

Review focus Ask the designer Inspect What makes the answer adequate?
Context Which site condition changed the proposal? Site plan plus the affected section or route Trace the condition to a visible spatial decision; identify an unresolved consequence.
Architectural integrity Where do programme, circulation and structure conflict? Coordinated plan/section and one junction Locate the conflict or show how it is resolved across drawings.
Environmental performance What improves relative to which alternative? Comparable options, actual output and assumptions State the measure, conditions and trade-off; keep the claim within the test.
Character Which design idea survives beyond the concept image? Diagram and its built-form consequence Point to the same idea in a plan, section or material decision.
Detail Which interface could undermine the intended quality? Detail appropriate to project stage Explain the issue and a feasible next drawing, test or specialist question.

Make the studio judgment explicit

Use a course action, with a reason:

  • Advance this aspect: the inspected evidence answers this question; retain the stated limit.
  • Revise this aspect: identify the drawing or decision that needs to change and the consequence it addresses.
  • Evidence needed: name the missing comparison, dimension, view, model assumption or observation.

These actions are not the council’s official recommendations. For a measured claim, record value, unit, rule source and margin where meaningful. For a qualitative claim, annotate the relevant feature and explain the stakeholder consequence. Do not turn preference into an invented numerical pass mark.

Finish with: one annotated drawing/result, a reasoned action, and one specific request that can be checked after revision. Continue on the practice card for the reviewer-led conversation, author response and A4 ledger entry.

| Actual scale | Meaning |
|---|---|

### Case A: layout generation — which metric is being improved?

Nauata et al. (2021), *House-GAN++: Generative Adversarial Layout Refinement Network towards Intelligent Computational Agent for Professional Architects*. [Official CVPR paper](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/papers/Nauata_House-GAN_Generative_Adversarial_Layout_Refinement_Network_towards_Intelligent_Computational_Agent_CVPR_2021_paper.pdf#page=8).

[Author preprint, Table 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.02574#page=8) is an alternate open reading link.

**Read:** metric definitions in §3 (p. 13634), protocol in §5 (p. 13636), and Table 2 (p. 13639). The slide reproduces the two **`Ours_dyna`** rows, labelled **`Divers.`** and **`Compat.`** in the paper. These compare dynamic refinement with different optimization targets. The reported ± is across-round standard deviation, not a confidence interval or a building pass mark.

**Course-authored reviewer task:** use both columns to explain the trade-off. Then choose one architectural requirement the table cannot establish—such as a usable circulation route—and specify the drawing or test you would need. Do not infer accessibility, daylight or construction feasibility from image/graph metrics alone.

Mora & Bardhan (2025), *Towards carbon neutrality: mapping mass retrofit opportunities in Cambridge, UK*, Royal Society Open Science 12:241337. **Definition check:** the main text does not fully specify the temperature reference used for ΔT. Do not rename it wall–air or indoor–outdoor difference. [Supplement Table S3](https://rs.figshare.com/collections/Supplementary_material_from_Towards_Carbon_Neutrality_Mapping_Mass_Retrofit_Opportunities_in_Cambridge_UK_/7618561) is a follow-up reading, not something this exercise has already verified.
